note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 25, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

The locally identified CDB90 English Parliamentary army uses a representative armoured pike component, following the National Army Museum’s surviving c.1640 pot helmet, cuirass, tassets and sidearm. Both parliamentary and royalist forces also fielded musketeers and other arms; this equipment assignment does not establish their proportions or an exact uniform. The local army identity, CDB90 personnel estimates and casualty categories remain unchanged.
